# Requirements Document: The photoid credential

## Introduction

The photoid holds the identity attributes of the holder, including a face
image (§4.1.1).  The guide takes its profile from ISO/IEC TS 23220-4 Annex C
and adds requirements of its own: the document type, which namespaces must be
present and which are recommended, and where the portrait comes from.  The
tables that list the data elements are in the ISO document, which this project
has not read, so the rules take them as a parameter.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneId/Photoid.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-id/blob/main/Rules/OneId/Photoid.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet. *Sources* lists the sections of the guide each rule was written from, *External specifications* lists the specifications it relies on and whether this project has read each, and *Confirmation* says whether anyone outside the model has confirmed the rule as written.

## Requirements

### Requirement OID-101

**User Story:** As a relying party, I want to know what every photoid I accept is sure to contain, so that I can build admissibility checks and face matching on it.

**Rule:** THE SYSTEM SHALL accept a credential as a photoid only when it meets every requirement the guide places on one. (Lean: `Photoid.violations`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.1 photoid](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §2 Terminology](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard)

**External specifications:** ISO/IEC TS 23220-4:2026, Annex C, §C.2.1 (not read); ISO/IEC TS 23220-4:2026, Annex C, Table C.1 (not read); ISO/IEC TS 23220-4:2026, Annex C, Table C.2 (not read); ISO/IEC TS 23220-4:2026, Annex C, Table C.3 (not read); ISO/IEC TS 23220-2:2026, §6.2.4 and its encoding rules (not read); ISO/IEC 18013-5:2021, §6.3.1, §8.3.1, §8.3.2 (not read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF the document type of a credential is not the photoid document type THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it as a photoid.
   - OID-101.1, proven: proven theorem `not_photoid_and_boardingPass`; proven theorem `photoid_docType`; example `documentTypes`
2. IF a photoid lacks the base identity namespace THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-101.2, proven: proven theorem `photoid_has_base`
3. IF a photoid lacks a data element that Table C.1 marks mandatory in the base identity namespace THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-101.3, proven: proven theorem `photoid_has_mandatory_base`
4. IF a data element of the base identity namespace does not have the encoding Table C.1 gives it THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the photoid.
   - OID-101.4, proven: proven theorem `photoid_base_encoding`; example `portraitInTheWrongEncoding`
5. IF a photoid has no portrait THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-101.5, open: open theorem `photoid_has_portrait`; example `photoidWithoutPortrait`
6. IF a photoid carries a namespace other than the three the guide lists, or a data element its table does not list THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-101.6, open: open theorem `photoid_only_listed`; example `photoidWithUnlistedData`
7. IF a photoid carries a portrait and a data group 2 that differ THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-101.7, open: open theorem `portrait_is_dg2`; example `portraitDiffersFromDataGroup`
8. IF a photoid carries the photoid namespace without a data element that Table C.2 marks mandatory THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-101.8, open: open theorem `photoid_nameSpace_complete`; example `photoidNameSpaceIncomplete`
9. IF a photoid carries the data groups namespace without a data element that Table C.3 marks mandatory THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-101.9, open: open theorem `dataGroups_nameSpace_complete`; example `dataGroupsNameSpaceIncomplete`

#### Open question on OID-101.5

> Every accepted photoid has a portrait.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide says the portrait MUST hold the
> image from the passport and that the business requirements need it, and it
> also refers the presence of every base element to Table C.1 of ISO/IEC TS
> 23220-4, which this project has not read.  If the table does not mark the
> portrait mandatory and the guide's sentence is read as a rule about the
> portrait's content only, a photoid with no face image is accepted.  The
> example `photoidWithoutPortrait` shows it.  Is the portrait mandatory in
> a One ID photoid, whatever Table C.1 says?

#### Open question on OID-101.6

> An accepted photoid carries only the three namespaces the guide lists, and
> in each only data elements its table lists.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide lists three namespaces for a
> photoid and refers to a table for each, and does not say the lists are closed.
> Under the reading that they are not, a photoid with a fourth namespace, or
> with a data element no table lists, is accepted, and a relying party that asks
> for the whole credential receives data the guide does not describe.  The
> example `photoidWithUnlistedData` shows it.  May a One ID photoid carry a
> namespace or a data element the guide and its tables do not list?

#### Open question on OID-101.7

> When an accepted photoid carries both a portrait and a data group 2, they
> are the same.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide says the portrait MUST hold "the
> dg2 or equivalent image data" from the passport and does not say what
> equivalent means or who checks it.  Under the reading that it is left to the
> issuer, a photoid whose portrait differs from its own data group 2 is
> accepted, so a touchpoint that matches a face against the portrait may be
> matching a different image from the one the data group holds.  The example
> `portraitDiffersFromDataGroup` shows it.  When a photoid carries data
> group 2, must the portrait be that image, and must a relying party check
> it?

#### Open question on OID-101.8

> When an accepted photoid carries the photoid namespace, the namespace
> holds every data element Table C.2 marks mandatory.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide recommends "this namespace and
> data elements presence" as in Table C.2 in one sentence.  Read as one
> recommendation, a photoid may carry the photoid namespace with any part of
> the travel document data missing, and a relying party that finds the
> namespace cannot count on any element in it.  The example
> `photoidNameSpaceIncomplete` shows it.  Once the photoid namespace is
> present, are the data elements Table C.2 marks mandatory required?

#### Open question on OID-101.9

> When an accepted photoid carries the data groups namespace, the namespace
> holds every data element Table C.3 marks mandatory.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide recommends the data groups
> namespace and "presence of the data elements" as in Table C.3 in one
> sentence, as it does for the photoid namespace.  Read as one recommendation, a
> photoid may carry the data groups namespace with any data group missing.  The
> example `dataGroupsNameSpaceIncomplete` shows it.  Once the data groups
> namespace is present, are the data elements Table C.3 marks mandatory
> required?

### Requirement OID-102

**User Story:** As an issuer, I want to know which recommendations of the guide a photoid I issue does not follow, so that I can decide whether to add the passport data a border authority may ask for later.

**Rule:** WHERE a photoid does not follow a recommendation of the guide THE SYSTEM SHALL report the recommendation. (Lean: `Photoid.advisories`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.1 photoid](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §2 Terminology](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard)

**External specifications:** ISO/IEC TS 23220-4:2026, Annex C, Table C.2 (not read); ISO/IEC TS 23220-4:2026, Annex C, Table C.3 (not read); ICAO Doc 9303, Part 10 (read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a photoid lacks the photoid namespace or the data groups namespace THE SYSTEM SHALL report each missing namespace as a recommendation it does not follow.
   - OID-102.1, proven: proven theorem `advises_dataGroups_nameSpace`; proven theorem `advises_photoid_nameSpace`; example `minimalPhotoid`
2. WHEN a photoid carries the photoid namespace without the image captured at enrolment THE SYSTEM SHALL report the missing image as a recommendation it does not follow.
   - OID-102.2, proven: proven theorem `advises_enrolment_portrait`
3. WHEN a photoid was derived from a document other than a passport THE SYSTEM SHALL report that as a recommendation it does not follow.
   - OID-102.3, proven: proven theorem `advises_source_document`; example `photoidFromAnIdentityCard`
4. WHEN a photoid lacks the photoid namespace or the data groups namespace THE SYSTEM SHALL report no broken requirement for the missing namespace.
   - OID-102.4, proven: proven theorem `recommended_nameSpace_never_required`; example `minimalPhotoid`

### Requirement OID-109

**User Story:** As a border authority, I want to know whether a photoid can come from a document other than a passport, so that I know what a photoid stands for when I check admissibility.

**Rule:** WHEN an issuer derives a photoid from an identity document THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the photoid only if the guide allows that kind of document. (Lean: `Photoid.sourceFindings`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §2 Terminology](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.1 photoid](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF a photoid was derived from a document other than a passport THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-109.1, open: open theorem `photoid_from_passport`; example `photoidFromAnIdentityCard`

#### Open question on OID-109.1

> A photoid the system accepts was derived from a passport.
>
> Open question for the business.  The terminology says a photoid can be
> derived from a passport or an equivalent identity document.  §4.1.1 says the
> values should always come from the passport, and that the portrait MUST hold
> image data sourced from the passport.  Under the reading that the first
> governs, a photoid derived from a national identity card is accepted, and
> nothing a relying party must receive says so.  The example
> `photoidFromAnIdentityCard` shows it.  May a One ID photoid be derived
> from a document other than a passport?
